html:
The campaign, around 727 BCE, in which Piye, king of Kush, marched north from Nubia and forced the rulers of Egypt to submit. It began the century of Kushite rule known as the 25th Dynasty.

For hundreds of years Egypt had ruled Nubia. By the 8th century BCE the tables had turned. Egypt was broken into small kingdoms in the Third Intermediate Period, while Kush was united and rich in gold.

When Tefnakhte of Sais, in the Delta, led a coalition south, Piye's army met it. It besieged the city of Hermopolis until its king surrendered, then stormed Memphis from the river. The Delta princes came to bow before Piye, and Tefnakhte sent his own oath of loyalty.

Piye did not stay. He made offerings at Egypt's great temples, left the local rulers in place and sailed home with tribute. His brother Shabaka completed the conquest, and kings from Napata ruled all Egypt as pharaohs. Their rule ended when Assyria invaded Egypt and sacked Thebes in 663 BCE, and the Kushites fell back south.
